shared_elements: shallow low-relief / incised carving on coarse, weathered stone
circular or ring-shaped motifs (carved ring on A, rounded hollows/cupules on B)
curved arcing lines forming band-like groupings
cluster of fine radiating/parallel linear strokes in the upper zone
largely undecorated expanse below the decorated upper area
justification: Both are eroded stone surfaces bearing shallow carved motifs concentrated in an upper zone — including fine radiating linear strokes and rounded/circular forms — above a comparatively empty lower expanse, which is the most specific correspondence. Against this, A is a freestanding, three-dimensionally shaped figural monolith with deliberately organised symmetrical relief (ring, arcing belts, head-and-body division), whereas B is a flat, irregular rock face whose marks are faint, scattered and partly natural-looking pitting, so the resemblance is generic rather than compositional.
